the witcher 3 is a gift that keeps on giving and remains my favourite game to this day. i started a new playthrough when the remaster update rolled out and ended up putting in 150+ hours. coming back to white orchard felt so nostalgic. this game is still one of the most beautiful and immersive worlds i've played, and toussaint looks absolutely stunning in the remaster. i didn't really play gwent the first time around, but got into it this time and it was so much fun. i don't usually do many side quests in games unless i need the xp or a specific item, but the stories behind the side quests in this game are so well written that they're hard to pass up. the choices you make throughout the game have lasting consequences, some of which don't reveal themselves until much later. the only real choice that matters is yen over triss. 

a few bugs still persist despite the remaster and all the hotfixes. the swamps in velen are one of the areas where you'll still run into the occasional bug and get stuck. even years after your first playthrough, you'll keep discovering new things about this game. it never really gets old, and i'd happily clock another 100 hours next time. props to cdpr for remastering a game that was already this good.

Played The Witcher 3 more times than I can count. All the way back in 2015 on PC(GOG) and I’ve also completed it on PS4. When I heard about the remaster and the new DLC coming out in 2027, I knew I had to go back one more time.

Having 100% completed it, I can now safely say this is easily one of the greatest games of all time. No one tells a story quite like CDPR and everyone should experience the Bloody Baron questline at least once in their life. There is truly nothing else like it.

That said, the remaster isn't without it's issues. Visual bugs pop up, environments(especially indoors) can be excessively dark and performance takes a hit with ray tracing or path tracing enabled. In Novigrad, the framerate drops to nearly half of what it is elsewhere in the game. Going for all the achievements was also a headache, particularly with Gwent cards tied to NPC's that occasionally become unresponsive. These bugs have been around since day one and have never been fixed.

Still, these are minor complaints for a game that remains pure joy.
The Witcher 3 is a fun game with a rich storyline, but its visuals and the flexibility of character controls are lacking.

Tried this game a few times before never got much further than White Orchard (early stage). The recent REMASTERED update gave me another chance. This time I succeeded. Finished the game including both DLC's. I never use QOL settings but for this game I did and that helped me finish the game. Did I like the game? Not really RPG's are not for me. What many people seem to like, the story and dialogue etc. It's way too much. The sheer amount of cutscenes and dialogue just gets in the way of proper pacing. TIP: don't play this on easy, you got serious no reason to roam the world and you will miss out on some proper quest design. Combat is mediocre at best. The mission structure of the main story is something else but quit a few quests are magical even near the end of the Blood and Wine DLC you'll still get suprises thrown at you and that was the reason I kept playing. Would I recommend this, well that depends if you like very heavy story driven games and complex inventory management go for this. If your like me you can skip this. 7/10
